solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pinned, as we are, stuck into desk working

indicators.note: one piece is stuck into the middle of the other, so it is placed inside
working here means operating in a new way, so the letters of desk are rearranged

parts.note: we are contracts to we're, spelt without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone describes being impaled, like the rest of us, on something jammed into a busy desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the desk letters to SKED, and 'stuck into' places the contraction we're, without its apostrophe, between SKE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered means fixed in place by a spike, a synonym of pinned.

clue.text: Got rid of loud female — nothing was uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
O is the zero digit, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone dismissed a noisy woman because nothing about her was cheering.
explanation.definitionFit: To saw off a limb is to remove it by cutting, so it is getting rid of something.

clue.text: Noise made by buzzer — end of sleep

parts.note: a bee is an insect that buzzes

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An alarm clock's buzz marks the end of a night's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzer' looks like an alarm clock, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A beep is a short high electronic sound, a kind of noise.

clue.text: Wife terribly nervy seeing monster

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of nervy are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A wife is very jumpy because she has seen a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a winged two-legged dragon of heraldry, a mythical monster.

clue.text: A frightful grunt when yours truly is involved in quarrel

indicators.note: one piece is involved in the other, so it sits inside it
frightful suggests the letters of grunt are put into a dreadful mess

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, the speaker

explanation.surface: A dreadful grunt erupts when I get dragged into a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' rearranges GRUNT to RGUNT after A, and 'is involved in' puts ME inside: ARGU-ME-NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a heated disagreement, a synonym of quarrel.

clue.text: Composer's drunk vodka penning end of lieder

definitions.note: read as composer is, a noun with the verb as link

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen encloses sheep, so one piece goes inside
drunk suggests the letters of vodka are reeling into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A composer gets tipsy on vodka while writing the last of his songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges VODKA to DVOAK, and 'penning' puts R (the last letter of lieder) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonin Dvorak was the Czech composer of the New World Symphony.

clue.text: Friend of everybody ending in ignominy

parts.note: all means everybody, every one of them

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A friend to everyone finishes up disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone on your side, a companion or supporter.

clue.text: King and knight associated with a terribly wicked practice

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
N is the chess notation for knight
terribly is used as an intensifier, meaning very

explanation.surface: Royalty and chivalry are linked with some truly evil goings-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' looks like an anagram signal, but it simply means VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is dishonest or roguish behaviour, the conduct of a scoundrel.

clue.text: Composer left after wild party

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a rave is a large lively party

explanation.surface: A composer departed once the riotous party was over.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero.

clue.text: Cry as TV doctor facing work

parts.note: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A shout goes up as a television doctor gets down to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a British TV series about a time-travelling alien called the Doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud excited shout, a kind of cry.

clue.text: English Queen to go wrong, having unknown royal assistant

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: An English queen blunders while her helper is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer who attends a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Mention school subject, and again, railing about it

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject

indicators.note: the railing goes about it, surrounding the other piece

parts.note: a fence is a railing or barrier
re- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Someone brings up a school subject and then, once more, complains about it.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education in British schools. 'railing' looks like complaining but is a barrier; 'about it' wraps it round the second RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference is a passing allusion to something, a synonym of mention.

clue.text: I jeer so inappropriately when Charlie comes in and is elated

indicators.note: one letter comes in, entering the other piece
inappropriately means the letters of the words are arranged wrongly

parts.note: Charlie is the radio alphabet word for C

explanation.surface: I mock rudely when Charlie walks in and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inappropriately' rearranges IJEERSO to REJOIES, and 'comes in' puts C inside: REJOI-C-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great joy, so it matches being elated.

clue.text: After end of work I quietly sleep

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: When the working day finishes, I quietly nod off.
explanation.definitionFit: Kip is British slang for a nap or sleep.

clue.text: Fade as apostle no longer favoured

parts.note: Peter was one of the twelve apostles
out means no longer in fashion or in favour

explanation.surface: An apostle loses his standing and slips from view.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to dwindle gradually to nothing, a synonym of fade.

clue.text: Mother wanting nuts sent around

indicators.note: sent around means turned back to front, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: nuts is slang for mad, crazy

explanation.surface: A mother who wants nuts sends them round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like food but means MAD; 'sent around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dam is the female parent of an animal, especially a horse.

clue.text: Poet marks one line — character slightly lacking

parts.note: M stands for the mark, the old German currency
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: slightly lacking means the word is missing a small bit, its final letter

parts.note: tone means the character or quality of something

explanation.surface: A critic grades a poet's every line, finding his character a little wanting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly lacking' drops the E from TONE to leave TON.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the English poet who wrote Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Most cheerful relation, one taken in by joke

indicators.note: being taken in by something means sitting inside it

parts.note: a jest is a joke
an aunt is a relation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The jolliest relative, a single person fooled by a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' looks like being fooled, but it means placed inside the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Jauntiest is the superlative of jaunty, lively and self-confident in manner.

clue.text: Expresses what guttersnipe is concealing

indicators.note: the word is concealing the letters, which run unbroken inside it

explanation.surface: A question about what a street urchin is hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to say it aloud, to express it in words.

clue.text: Woman embraced by strangest hero

indicators.note: embraced by means the letters are held within the run of these words

explanation.surface: A woman is held in the arms of a most unusual hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a woman's name, also the biblical queen.

clue.text: Musician is beginning to talk with coterie

parts.note: a cell is a small close group, a coterie

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musician starts chatting with an exclusive clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist plays the cello, so is a musician.

clue.text: Young animal going over a West Indian island

indicators.note: in a down clue, the young animal goes over, above, the other piece

parts.note: a cub is a young bear, fox or lion

explanation.surface: A young beast crosses over to a Caribbean isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island of the Caribbean, in the West Indies.

clue.text: Mum's right to follow friend

definitions.note: read as mum is, a noun with the verb as link

indicators.note: to follow means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Mother is justified in tagging along behind a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, old-fashioned British public-school slang for one's mum.

clue.text: Seductive woman in furs, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the word is said and heard

parts.note: minks are furs made from the pelts of the mink

explanation.surface: A temptress dressed in furs, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a flirtatious, impudent girl, a coquette.

clue.text: Shouts disapprovingly, being heard finding alcohol

indicators.note: being heard means the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: boos are shouts of disapproval

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers on finding someone has been drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is informal for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Our dean arranged a piece of music

indicators.note: arranged, as music is arranged, means the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Our cathedral dean scored a piece for choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' plays on musical arrangement while rearranging OURDEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a medieval French song form with a refrain, the forerunner of the rondo.
